processes.description: Customers such as a utility's fuel and plant buyer and a gas company contact email the logistics contact asking for prices on a stated volume at a delivery point, or for hedges, swaps or fixed forward purchases. The recipient does not price these: the request is forwarded to the colleague who handles customer pricing, or a colleague is asked to call the customer that day. That person checks with the traders for a quote or bid and takes it back to the customer, who replies asking for a call to go over it.
steps: A customer emails a request for a price on a stated gas volume and delivery point, or for a hedge, swap or fixed forward purchase.
The recipient forwards the request to the colleague who handles pricing, or asks a colleague to call the customer.
That person checks with the traders for a quote or bid.
The quote is given back to the customer by phone or email.
The customer replies and asks for a call to go over the quote.

stalls.summary: Requests reach someone who does not price them and are passed along: one is forwarded on a colleague's suggestion, another comes with a plea to call the customer that day, and a customer asks the recipient to go and check with the traders, so each quote waits on a hand-off before anyone prices it.
The customer's reply thanks the desk for its patience and asks for a call to go over the quote, so the round closes only after a further conversation, and the same follow-up recurs.

automation.approach: A standard quote-request message or form that captures product, volume, delivery point, term and the date a reply is needed, routed straight to the trading desk contact, with an indicative price pulled from the current curve for the trader to confirm before calling the customer.
automation.rationale: Requests arrive with the logistics contact and get forwarded around before a trader sees them, and the recipient has to go back to the traders for the terms. A template that carries every term in one message gets the request to the right person complete; setting the price and talking to the customer stay with people.

work_estimate.rationale: The hands-on part of a round is getting a price: reading the request's volume, point and term, checking with the traders for a quote or bid, and talking the customer through it on the phone. That is short for a simple delivered-gas quote and longer for a hedge or fixed forward structure, so 10 to 45 minutes with 20 as the middle. A request template and a curve lookup could take over gathering the terms and an indicative price; the trader's price and the customer call stay manual.

processes.description: Real-time desk staff send service customers their models for each flow date: the EPE model for El Paso Electric and the EES model spreadsheets, with EES hourly data available to add to the daily mail-out. Bill Williams III runs the distribution: he forwards the EES models, asks for names to be added to or removed from the EES list, corrects mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams, and requires the EPE Reconciliation sheet to be completed even when there are no variances, following up on where the new reconciliation model lives.
steps: Real-time staff complete the EPE model or the EES model spreadsheets for the flow date.
They complete the EPE Reconciliation sheet, even when there are no variances.
They add the EES hourly data to the mail-out where the recipient wants it.
They email the model and sheets to the customer's recipient list.
Copies of the EES model are forwarded to internal staff who follow it.
The recipient list is updated when names are added or removed or mail reaches the wrong person.
The desk lead follows up when a sheet is missing or a model's location changes.

stalls.summary: The EPE reconciliation sheet was not done, and the desk lead had to instruct that it be completed even when there are no variances.
The recipient lists go wrong: mail goes to the wrong Bill Williams, he has to confirm he is listed as Bill Williams III, and names have to be added to and removed from the EES list.
A new EPE Reconciliation Model needed a follow-up message so that everyone knew where it is kept and what state it is in.

automation.approach: Generate the EPE and EES models, the hourly data and the reconciliation sheet from the deal data on a schedule, send them to one distribution list keyed by email address and kept by one owner, and add a check that holds the mail-out when the reconciliation sheet is blank.
automation.rationale: The problems the mail shows are a skipped reconciliation sheet, a moved model file and wrong recipients, not the building of the model itself. A short mail-out checklist covering the model, the reconciliation sheet even with no variances, the hourly data and the current recipient list addresses those first; scheduling the export and send then removes the repetitive attach-and-send.

work_estimate.rationale: A round is filling in and checking the day's EPE or EES model, completing the EPE reconciliation sheet against any variances, attaching hourly data and keeping the recipient list right. A round that is only a list change takes about 5 minutes, a normal model round about 15, and one with variances to reconcile up to 40. Building, attaching and sending the files to a maintained list can be scheduled, and a check can flag a blank reconciliation sheet; reviewing variances stays manual.

processes.description: Deals are moved between risk books on request. Before the bankruptcy, the west region's controller sends book runners lists of deals to flip, such as index deals out of FT-WEST or deals from MGMT-WEST, G-DAILY-EST and INTRA-EMWMEH into FT-US/CAND-ERMS, often due that day, and asks them to sweep their books for leftovers. After the ENA filings, several staff send lists of terminated counterparties and auto-terminating deals to move into bankruptcy books in TAGG and zero out in Sitara, with book renames and some moves back to the live side.
steps: A controller or the bankruptcy team identifies deals to move, from a book reorganisation or a counterparty termination list.
The deal list is sent or forwarded to the book's runner with the target book and often a deadline.
The runner moves or flips each listed deal to the target book.
For bankruptcy moves, the deals go to the bankruptcy book in TAGG and are zeroed out going forward in Sitara.
The book is calculated and officialized again after the move.
Moved deals are cross-referenced against the termination list and the book's calcs.
The runner confirms the flip; deals found later are sent on as follow-up lists of stragglers.
Deals moved in error are moved back from the bankruptcy book to the live side.

stalls.summary: Termination lists arrive piecemeal: one participant is still waiting on a final list to cross-reference with calcs while further lists of more deals and stragglers keep arriving, so the same books are reopened round after round.

Deals left in old books turn up after the main move: a last deal in the FT-Northwest book, one more deal found to flip, and requests to go into all books or make sure all Canadian deals have moved show sweeps after the fact.
Reconciling a book against what another party holds needs outside help and the exact deal terms, and the approach is changed to a simpler fix.
Some transactions placed in the bankruptcy book are later asked to go back to the live side, undoing an earlier move.

contradictions.summary: Who owns the bankruptcy terminations is stated differently: one message says Darron and the writer will handle terminations from that day on while Scott heads another project, a later one names Greg Couch as leading the estate risk effort, and move lists keep coming from other senders as well.

Instructions on where terminated deals go change during the bankruptcy moves: one request moves named counterparties from NG-Price to Bankruptcy, a later one says to move deals with the FT-TERMIN-GD book instead of booking counterparty FT-CAND-TERMIN, and another renames NG-Price to ENA-FT-WC-SJ.

automation.approach: One standard deal-move list (deal number, counterparty, current book, target book, effective date, systems to update) feeding a bulk transfer; a query that pulls every deal of a terminated counterparty across all books so stragglers surface at once; and a post-move check that compares book totals and flags deals still sitting in old books.
automation.rationale: Requests arrive as ad hoc lists in different shapes from different senders, deals left behind surface later, and some moves are reversed. One list layout that every requester fills in, matched against a counterparty query, cuts the stragglers and misreads; the moves themselves and the cross-check against calcs are the repetitive parts a tool can take on, while deciding which deals belong where stays with people.

work_estimate.rationale: A round means finding the listed deals, moving each to the target book in TAGG, zeroing bankruptcy deals out in Sitara, recalculating and officializing the book, and cross-checking against the termination list or calcs. Lists run from a single deal to several counterparties' deals, so 10 to 90 minutes with about 30 in the middle. A counterparty query and bulk move could select and move most deals and compare book totals afterwards; deciding which deals belong where and handling stragglers and reversals stays with people.
